results.title: Use API Keys to Authenticate Endpoint Requests | Klaviyo Developers
results.snippet:
Klaviyo provides 3 methods of authentication including private key authentication and OAuth (used to call server-side APIs) and public key authentication (used to call client-side APIs). Read the table below to learn more about how each method can be used for authenticating API calls:
| Server-side APIs | | Client-side APIs |
|---|---|---|
| Private key authentication All /api endpoints use API private keys to authenticate requests. If you do not use an API key for your requests, or if you use a key from the wrong account, your call will return an error. A 400 error indicates an invalid or missing API key. | OAuth If you are a tech partner integrating with Klaviyo, we recommend using OAuth to [make authorized API calls](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/set_up_oauth). OAuth offers multiple benefits over a private key integration, including security, usability, improved rate limits, and the ability to be listed in Klaviyo's App Marketplace. | Public key authentication All /client endpoints use a public API key: your 6-character company ID, also known as a site ID. We recommend using the [Klaviyo object](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/introduction_to_the_klaviyo_object)

results.title: Migrate to OAuth from private key authentication
results.snippet:
If you’re here, it’s likely that your Klaviyo app uses private key authentication. We now require all of our published partners to use OAuth when integrating with Klaviyo.

Switching your app from private key authentication to OAuth allows for greater exposure to our customers, simpler integration workflows, and access to all new items our R&D team is developing.

- **Exclusive API access**
Unlock powerful API features, including our Universal Content and Webhooks APIs.

If your app was previously published using private key authentication, we estimate that a single engineer will need 1-2 sprints (2-4 weeks) to complete the migration to OAuth. When migrating to OAuth, each step listed below should take roughly 1 week:
1. **OAuth implementation**
- [Create your OAuth app](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/create_a_public_oauth_app). Please note that after creation, your app will require at least 5 active users to meet our listing requirements before submission.
- Ensure you properly handle refresh tokens and token expiration.
- Start completing our [Testing & Review Template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_KiNf2HnmiPujtmoSctrQIUWswhIRYfQNZaOMq-Rktg/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.

It supports **SMS** and **WhatsApp** channels — the channel is determined automatically based on the conversation. results.title: How to create or clone a private API key | Klaviyo Help Center
results.snippet:
When you create a private API key, choose an access level for each API scope. These access levels determine whether a third party can:
- Have no access to the data or actions covered by that scope.
- View data covered by that scope without making changes (read access).
- View data and create, delete, or make other changes covered by that scope (read/write access).
For example, to subscribe profiles to marketing and add them to a Klaviyo list from another application, use [Bulk Subscribe Profiles](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/reference/bulk_subscribe_profiles). This endpoint requires `lists:write`, `profiles:write`, and `subscriptions:write`. Granting read/write access for these scopes covers this request; you do not need to grant access to unrelated scopes.

- After you create a private API key, you cannot:
- View the full private API key again after leaving its confirmation page.
- Tip: securely save private API keys and note down what you want to use them for, such as in a password manager.
- Add or edit its scopes.

results.title: Campaigns API overview (omnichannel)
results.snippet:
Machine-readable spec for the Campaigns API: [stable/categories/campaigns.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaviyo/openapi/main/openapi/stable/categories/campaigns.json)

The Campaigns API is organized into five endpoint groups:
- **Campaigns** — Create, retrieve, update, delete, and clone campaigns.
- **Campaign Audiences** — Manage targeted audience segments within a campaign, with priority ordering.
- **Campaign Messages** — Configure and schedule individual sends within an audience.
- **Campaign Variations** — Define per-channel content (email, SMS, push, WhatsApp) for each message.
- **Scheduling** — Schedule all messages at once or individually, with support for multiple send strategies.

results.title: Klaviyo MCP server
results.snippet:
The Klaviyo Model Context Protocol (MCP) server seamlessly integrates with Klaviyo’s APIs, enabling AI clients to interact with your Klaviyo data. This guide will walk you through configuring various MCP clients for both the remote-hosted MCP server (recommended) and the local MCP server.
##
What is MCP?
[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) (Model Context Protocol) is an open protocol that helps AI models securely interface with different data sources and tools. You’ll connect Klaviyo’s MCP server to an MCP client, i.e., an AI agent like Claude or Cursor, to get assistance with your Klaviyo data. Your MCP client can help with a [variety of tasks](/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server#available-tools) from campaign creation to flow performance reports.

>
> This feature is only available to Klaviyo users with an Owner, Admin, or Manager role. Learn more about [Klaviyo user roles](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005231648).

results.title: Klaviyo MCP Server: Analyze Performance & Build Campaigns With AI - Klaviyo
results.snippet:
The Klaviyo MCP server connects compatible AI clients to Klaviyo APIs through an authorized Model Context Protocol connection. It supports permitted reporting and account actions, with configurable tools, scopes, and access controls.

- **Flexible client support:** Documented connection options include Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, and other compatible remote MCP clients.
---
## What is the Klaviyo MCP server?
The Klaviyo MCP server connects compatible AI clients to Klaviyo APIs through Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP is an open protocol that helps AI models securely interface with data sources and tools.
The server gives an AI client a defined set of Klaviyo tools. Depending on the tools and permissions available, you can ask the client to retrieve campaign results, compare flow performance, or create a campaign.
### Why the Klaviyo MCP server matters
An AI client needs an authorized connection before it can work with data or tools in your Klaviyo account. The Klaviyo MCP server provides that connection, so the client can handle supported requests based on the access you approve.

results.title: Klaviyo MCP Server Guide For Agencies | Klaviyo Help Center
results.snippet:
The Klaviyo MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is a secure bridge that lets AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT connect directly to Klaviyo. Once connected, you can talk to your Klaviyo account in plain language: ask questions, pull reports, analyze performance, and draft or create campaigns and templates, without logging into the dashboard and exporting data by hand.
Under the hood it is a wrapper on top of Klaviyo's APIs. You authorize each account separately, and the AI assistant can then read that account's data and take supported actions within the permissions you grant.

To connect an account you will need:
- **An Owner, Admin, or Manager role** on each Klaviyo account you want to connect.
- **A Claude or ChatGPT account.** Connecting several accounts (custom connector) requires a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise) or ChatGPT developer mode. *This guide covers Claude setup.*
- For Claude Team or Enterprise, someone with permission to add custom connectors must first add the connector to your organization. Members then connect it to their own Klaviyo accounts. See [Claude’s custom connector setup instructions](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-ge

results.title: developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server_available_tools
results.snippet:
The Klaviyo MCP server exposes over 300 tools that your MCP client can call to interact with your Klaviyo data. The tools are grouped by category below. For each tool, the table shows whether it is read-only, whether it reads user-generated content, and whether it is available on the remote-hosted server.
Use the columns to understand how each tool behaves:
* **Read Only** — the tool only reads data and can't modify your Klaviyo account. These tools remain available when `read-only=true` (remote) or `READ_ONLY=true` (local) is set.
* **Has User Generated Content** — the tool reads user-generated content (e.g., profile properties, event data, or reviews) that could be interpreted by your LLM. These tools are disabled when `disable-tools-with-user-generated-content=true` (remote) or `ALLOW_USER_GENERATED_CONTENT=false` (local) is set. Be sure to carefully review each tool call to ensure your client is not acting on malicious instructions.
* **Available on Remote Server** — the tool is available on the [remote-hosted server](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/connect_to_the_klaviyo_mcp_server#configure-your-mcp-client-for-the-remote-hosted-server-recommended). Tools without a chec
